predecessors.name: Papal States
predecessors.text: Ferrara and its domains, 'about 1,100 km2 south of the lower Po River'

successors.name: Duchy of Modena and Reggio
successors.text: Modena and Reggio, kept by Cesare d'Este

ledger.x: 1208: Azzo VI d'Este becomes lord of Ferrara.
1438: Venice's first hold on Rovigo ends.
1471: Borso d'Este is made Duke of Ferrara by Pope Paul II.
1482: Venice goes to war with Ferrara.
7 August 1484: the Treaty of Bagnolo makes the loss final.
7 August 1484: Bagnolo ends the War of Ferrara.
1509: the Este recover Rovigo in the War of the League of Cambrai.
1514: Venice takes Rovigo back for good.
1597: the Este lose Ferrara to the papacy.
1597: the Duchy of Ferrara ends when the pope takes the vacant fief; the Este keep Modena and Reggio.

wars.name: War of Ferrara
wars.outcome: Venice took Rovigo (capitulated 17 August 1482) and besieged Ferrara from November 1482; the Treaty of Bagnolo (7 August 1484) left Venice 'the town of Rovigo and a broad swath of the fertile delta of the Po'.

wars.name: War of the League of Cambrai
wars.outcome: The Este recovered Rovigo during the war; Venice returned in 1514 and kept it to 1797.

wars.name: Devolution of Ferrara
wars.outcome: Alfonso II d'Este died childless in October 1597; Clement VIII raised an army, excommunicated Cesare d'Este and took Ferrara; Cesare entered Modena in January 1598.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; Ferrara is a radius round the city, Rovigo a province, and only the Treaty of Bagnolo (1484) is a dated line.
